title: Hardball Tactics
description: Recognising the standard pressure plays — and what to do about them.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Some negotiators rely on pressure rather than persuasion: extreme openings, take-it-or-leave-it threats, good-cop-bad-cop, and last-minute "nibbling" for extras. They work only if you do not name them.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: These tactics create stress and urgency, which shortens thinking and pushes people toward a quick yes. Naming them out loud removes most of their power.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: A colleague playing the unreasonable one while another plays reasonable.
Asking for one more small extra after everything is agreed.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Pressure applied at the last minute.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Recognise the tactic, name it calmly, and slow down. "It sounds like we're being asked to decide under pressure" is often enough.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: A sudden shift in tone late in the process.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Never accept a deadline you cannot verify.
Refuse to add extras after agreement without reopening the whole deal.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Conceding to make the pressure stop.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Name the tactic to defuse it.
Slow down when you feel rushed.
